article_content: Manchester United are ramping up efforts to secure West Ham's highly-touted 15-year-old defender Reece Oxford, facing competition from Arsenal and Chelsea. The imposing center-back, who turns 16 in December, has showcased his abilities both for West Ham's U21 side and as captain of England's U17 squad. While West Ham have presented a lucrative contract extension, the teenager remains non-committal amid growing interest. Arsenal's scouts were recently spotted observing Oxford during a U21 match against Sunderland, continuing their long-term monitoring of the defender. Manchester United's recruitment team views Oxford as a superior prospect compared to their current young defenders and have accelerated youth acquisitions, including the signing of Ajax's Timothy Fosu-Mensah and pursuing Norwegian wonderkid Martin Odegaard. Potential departure of Oxford would deal a dual blow to West Ham, both competitively and financially, with compensation limited to £250,000 under youth player regulations. Co-chairman David Sullivan recently lamented the challenges of retaining academy talents, stating: 'It nearly makes you question the purpose of maintaining youth systems when rivals can poach your best 15-year-olds.'

article_content: Two Gonzaga University seniors face disciplinary measures ranging from suspension to expulsion after using a legally-owned firearm to ward off an intruder in their university-managed apartment. The October 24 confrontation began when a man recently released from jail knocked on their door demanding cash. Erik Fagan described to local press how his instincts signaled danger as the individual forced entry, prompting roommate Daniel McIntosh to retrieve a family-inherited handgun, which scared the intruder away. University officials confirmed the students violated campus weapon policies, though the apartment complex lacks security gates or keycard requirements. Campus security seized both the defensive pistol and Fagan's hunting shotgun during a 2 AM visit following police apprehension of the six-time convicted felon. While Washington state allows concealed carry with permits, Gonzaga prohibits weapons in all university-affiliated properties. Attorney Dean Chuang noted the disciplinary panel (comprising three faculty and two students) found policy violations, despite both seniors' clean records. One student reportedly didn't know the housing rules applied, while the other believed off-campus residences were exempt. President Thayne McCulloh has initiated campus-wide discussions to re-examine firearm policies, maintaining existing conduct codes during the review period.

article_content: Britain's oldest person - and the last survivor of the Victorian era - has passed away at 114. Ethel Lang witnessed six monarchs and 22 prime ministers during her lifetime. Born on May 27, 1900, she was recognized as the world's eighth oldest person. Mrs. Lang's life spanned pivotal events including the Wright Brothers' first flight (1903), both World Wars, the Russian Revolution (1917), the 1929 Wall Street Crash, Moon landings, and the internet's creation. She was 11 during the Titanic sinking and 101 during the 9/11 attacks. The Water Royd House care home in Barnsley confirmed her passing. Her daughter Margaret Bates (91) recalled: 'She remained curious about life despite blindness from 1988. She hated being confined indoors.' Married to plumber William Lang in 1922, she lived independently until 105. Her hobbies included dancing until age 107 and watching snooker. Family attributes her longevity to healthy habits, home-cooked meals, and genetic predisposition. Following London resident Grace Jones' death at 113 in 2013, Mrs. Lang held the 'oldest Briton' title. Gladys Hooper (turning 112 tomorrow) now assumes this status. The world's oldest living person is Japan's Misao Okawa, who will celebrate her 117th birthday in March.

article_content: (CNN) -- A former Pennsylvania juvenile court judge received a 28-year prison sentence Thursday for operating a scheme that unjustly incarcerated minors for financial gain, according to court records. Mark Ciavarella, former Luzerne County judge, was additionally ordered to pay approximately $1 million in restitution by a federal court. This sentence quadruples the initial 87-month term proposed in Ciavarella's 2009 plea deal, which a judge later rejected, leading to trial. In February, Ciavarella was convicted on 12 of 39 counts including racketeering and fraud for accepting $2.8 million in bribes from private detention center operators. The case gained national attention following an emotional 2011 confrontation with Sandy Fonzo, whose 17-year-old son Edward Kenzakowski received a six-month detention sentence for drug paraphernalia possession despite having no prior record. Fonzo testified that her son never recovered from the incarceration trauma and died by suicide three years later. 'He destroyed my child's spirit,' Fonzo shouted during the courthouse encounter filmed by news crews. She expressed outrage upon learning Ciavarella wouldn't be immediately jailed after conviction, screaming: 'Do you remember my son? He shot himself because of you!'

article_content: Kathleen Danby, 72, received a three-month jail sentence from the Court of Protection in April after embracing her 19-year-old granddaughter against social services' directives. The grandmother was arrested during a Ken Dodd comedy performance at Liverpool Philharmonic Hall on Sunday night and remains in custody. Police confirmed she'll appear in court today. The granddaughter, who has learning difficulties, was placed in care in Derbyshire in 2007. Family members face strict contact restrictions, with Mrs. Danby limited to monthly monitored calls. A February 2023 breach occurred when they met at a model railway exhibition, with CCTV later showing an embrace outside a pub. Judge Martin Cardinal stated contact with family increases the young woman's distress, justifying the imprisonment for contempt. This follows the 2012 case of Wanda Maddocks, who was jailed without public disclosure for removing her father from care. Current rules require public naming of imprisoned individuals. Family members and advocates criticize the proceedings' secrecy. The granddaughter's father, prohibited from contact since 2006 after a child safety incident, faces arrest warrants for attempted communication. Mrs. Danby states her granddaughter has left care facilities over 170 times seeking family contact.

article_content: German artist Wolfgang Stiller has created an evocative exhibition titled 'Matchstick Men,' featuring sculptures resembling oversized matches with darkened human faces. The site-specific installation emerged from experiments with leftover art materials and bamboo molds of Chinese faces during studio work in various international locations including New York and Beijing. Stiller used thick lumber pieces to create matchstick-like sculptures, complete with bent, warped, and burnt elements alongside large-scale matchboxes. The exhibition, not designed as traveling show, will remain at Zurich's Python Gallery until April 20, 2013 as part of the 'Burnout' showcase. The 52-year-old artist emphasizes open interpretation: 'While all faces used are Chinese, this isn't specific criticism. The metaphor applies to any system. The matchboxes could represent coffins or remain simple formal elements. I prefer art that invites personal imagination,' stated Stiller, who has resided in New York, Shanghai, Beijing, and Berlin.

article_content: Manchester United protected their narrow Premier League lead with a rapid-fire victory against West Ham on Wednesday. Dutch forward Robin van Persie stunned spectators by scoring within 33 seconds - the fastest goal this season - through a deflected shot assisted by Michael Carrick. Manager Alex Ferguson highlighted defensive improvements as crucial for title hopes after the 1-0 triumph. Manchester City stayed close behind with a 2-0 win at Wigan. Mario Balotelli's second-half breakthrough (his first since returning to the lineup) and James Milner's long-range finish secured points, though manager Roberto Mancini expressed dissatisfaction with Balotelli's overall performance. Chelsea's interim manager Rafael Benitez faced continued challenges with a goalless draw against Fulham, marking his third consecutive match without scoring. Home fans voiced disapproval as Chelsea remains seven points behind league leaders. article_content: An Iraqi lawmaker was killed in a suicide bombing during a public visit in central Falluja on Tuesday, authorities reported. Ayfan Sadoon al-Essawi, member of the secular al-Iraqiya coalition, died with two others when an assailant posing as a laborer detonated an explosive vest after embracing him at a construction site. Four individuals sustained injuries in the attack. The late legislator, former head of Falluja's Awakening Council and a tribal leader, had survived previous assassination attempts. Islamic State of Iraq had listed him as a wanted target. UN Special Representative Martin Kobler condemned the 'brutal killing,' urging political factions to avoid sectarian conflict. In a separate incident, Finance Minister Rafie al-Essawi (unrelated to the deceased) avoided injury when a roadside bomb exploded near his convoy west of Baghdad on Monday. Both officials belong to the al-Iraqiya bloc led by former Prime Minister Ayad Allawi.

article_content: Crystal Palace goalkeeper Julian Speroni is celebrating both family joy and club pride following the birth of his daughter Isabella. The photoshoot carried special significance, with images captured by Kels Noades - daughter of late Crystal Palace chairman Ron Noades, who oversaw the club's historic achievements including their 1990 FA Cup final appearance, third-place First Division finish, and 1991 Zenith Data Systems Cup victory. Speroni, who recently faced challenges in matches against Hull City, now prepares for Saturday's Premier League clash against Chelsea striker Diego Costa. Despite new parenting responsibilities, the veteran goalkeeper remains focused on maintaining Palace's strong season start under manager Neil Warnock.

article_content: (CNN) -- The space shuttle Atlantis completed a successful landing Friday morning under clear skies at Florida's Kennedy Space Center. The seven-member crew concluded an 11-day mission delivering essential components to extend the International Space Station's operational lifespan. Astronaut Nicole Stott returned alongside six colleagues after her 87-day stay aboard the ISS. 'Couldn't have chosen a better day,' remarked Commander Charles Hobaugh during descent. Mission Control praised the landing as a 'flawless conclusion' to the mission, specifically welcoming Stott's Earth return. Post-landing procedures included medical checks via a specialized transport vehicle equipped with rest facilities. The mission featured three spacewalks and installation of storage platforms for future maintenance parts. These components will support station operations after NASA retires its shuttle fleet next year. Critical systems addressed include thermal regulation and orbital stability mechanisms. Crew members celebrated Thanksgiving in orbit with traditional holiday foods. Notably, astronaut Randy Bresnik became the second NASA crew member to have a child born during a mission, with his daughter weighing 6 pounds, 13 ounces. Russia will assume primary resupply responsibilities for the ISS moving forward.

article_content: The upcoming Broadway revival of Ibsen's 'An Enemy of the People,' starring Jeremy Strong, has added two significant collaborators: Michael Imperioli will co-star, and Plan B Entertainment (founded by Brad Pitt, Dede Gardner, and Jeremy Kleiner) joins as producer. This production marks Broadway debuts for both Imperioli and Plan B. Full casting details will be announced later. As previously announced, the 16-week limited engagement begins previews at Broadway's Circle in the Square Theatre on February 27, 2024, with an official opening on March 18. The new adaptation by Tony-nominated playwright Amy Herzog ('A Doll's House') will be directed by Tony Award winner Sam Gold ('Fun Home'). Imperioli, currently starring in Hulu's 'The Fool,' received an Emmy nomination for Season 2 of 'The White Lotus' and is best known for his six-season role as Christopher Moltisanti in HBO's 'The Sopranos.' While having Off-Broadway experience, this marks his Broadway debut. Plan B Entertainment joins lead producers Seaview and Patrick Catullo in this Broadway debut. Seaview's notable productions include 'Parade,' 'The Sign in Sidney Brustein's Window,' and Mike Birbiglia's 'The Old Man & the Pool.' Their upcoming projects feature collaborations with artists like Rachel Chavkin and Sufjan Stevens. In Herzog's adaptation, Strong plays a small-town doctor who risks community backlash after exposing a public health crisis that his neighbors seek to conceal.

article_content: The burden of heat-related mortality during Europe's 2022 summer may have exceeded 70,000 deaths according to a study led by the Barcelona Institute for Global Health (ISGlobal). Published in The Lancet Regional Health—Europe, researchers revised upward initial estimates of temperature-related deaths. Their study titled 'The Effect of Temporal Data Aggregation to Assess the Impact of Changing Temperatures in Europe: An Epidemiological Modelling Study' addresses methodological limitations in prior research. Previous work in Nature Medicine estimated 62,862 heat-related deaths using weekly temperature and mortality data from 823 regions. Researchers acknowledged weekly data's tendency to underestimate mortality impacts compared to daily data. The new study developed a theoretical framework analyzing errors from aggregated data (weekly/monthly) versus daily data using records from 147 regions across 16 countries. Analysis revealed aggregation time scales significantly affect estimates: weekly models underestimated heat-related mortality by 21.56% and cold-related deaths by 8.56% compared to daily models during 1998-2004. During extreme events like 2003's heatwave, weekly data's underestimation reduced to 4.62%. Applying this framework to 2022 data showed prior estimates underestimated heat deaths by 10.28%, revising the total to 70,066 deaths. Lead researcher Joan Ballester Claramunt noted: 'Weekly data remains valuable for real-time epidemiological surveillance despite underestimation trends. When daily data isn't available, weekly aggregates provide a practical approximation for public health responses like heatwave emergency plans.' The team emphasizes balancing methodological precision with bureaucratic realities of large-scale data collection.

'தற்காலிக தரவு ஒருங்கிணைப்பின் விளைவு: ஐரோப்பாவில் மாறும் வெப்பநிலையின் தாக்க மதிப்பீட்டிற்கான தொற்றுநோயியல் மாதிரி ஆய்வு' எனும் இந்த ஆய்வு முந்தைய ஆராய்ச்சிகளின் முறைமை வரம்புகளை உள்ளடக்கியது. நேச்சர் மெடிசின் இதழில் முன்னர் வெளியான ஆய்வு, 823 பிராந்தியங்களின் வாராந்திர வெப்பநிலை மற்றும் இறப்பு தரவுகளைக் கொண்டு 62,862 வெப்பம் சார்ந்த இறப்புகளை மதிப்பிட்டது. ஆராய்ச்சியாளர்கள் தினசரி தரவுகளுடன் ஒப்பிடும்போது வாராந்திர தரவுகள் இறப்பு தாக்கங்களைக் குறைத்து மதிப்பிடும் என ஏற்றுக்கொண்டனர். புதிய ஆய்வு 16 நாடுகளின் 147 பிராந்தியங்களின் பதிவுகளைப் பயன்படுத்தி, தினசரி தரவுகளுடன் ஒப்பிடும்போது ஒருங்கிணைக்கப்பட்ட தரவுகளிலிருந்து (வாராந்திர/மாதாந்திர) ஏற்படும் பிழைகளைப் பகுப்பாய்வு செய்ய ஒரு கோட்பாட்டுக் கட்டமைப்பை உருவாக்கியது. பகுப்பாய்வு வெளிப்படுத்தியது: 1998-2004 காலத்தில் தினசரி மாதிரிகளுடன் ஒப்பிடும்போது வாராந்திர மாதிரிகள் வெப்பம் சார்ந்த இறப்புகளை 21.56% மற்றும் குளிர் சார்ந்த இறப்புகளை 8.56% குறைத்து மதிப்பிட்டன. 2003 வெப்ப அலை போன்ற தீவிர நிகழ்வுகளில் வாராந்திர தரவுகளின் குறை மதிப்பீடு 4.62% ஆகக் குறைந்தது. 2022 தரவுகளுக்கு இக்கட்டமைப்பைப் பயன்படுத்தியதில், முந்தைய மதிப்பீடுகள் வெப்ப இறப்புகளை 10.28% குறைத்து மதிப்பிட்டதாகக் கண்டறியப்பட்டு, மொத்தம் 70,066 இறப்புகள் என திருத்தப்பட்டது. தலைமை ஆராய்ச்சியாளர் ஜோன் பாலெஸ்டர் க்ளாரமண்ட் விளக்கினார்: 'குறை மதிப்பீடு இருந்தபோதிலும், வாராந்திர தரவுகள் நிகழ்நேர தொற்றுநோய்க்கான கண்காணிப்பில் பயனுள்ளதாக உள்ளன. தினசரி தரவு கிடைக்காத போது, வாராந்திரத் தரவுகள் வெப்ப அலை அவசரத் திட்டங்கள் போன்ற பொது சுகாதார நடவடிக்கைகளுக்கு நடைமுறைத் தீர்வாக அமைகின்றன.' பெரிய அளவிலான தரவு சேகரிப்பின் நிர்வாகச் சவால்களுடன் முறைமைத் துல்லியத்தை சமப்படுத்துவதை ஆய்வுக் குழு வலியுறுத்துகிறது.

article_content: Paris, France (CNN) -- France's foreign ministry confirmed Thursday that a photograph showing seven hostages in Niger - including five French citizens - has been authenticated, calling it an 'encouraging sign' confirming their survival. The ministry stated: 'While the photo's capture date remains unclear, it shows all hostages alive as of September 30. All government resources are engaged to secure their release.' The image appeared on an al Qaeda-associated website alongside audio recordings purportedly featuring hostages answering questions from an unidentified interrogator. Al Qaeda in the Islamic Maghreb (AQIM) claimed responsibility for abducting the group, which includes six men and one woman employed by French nuclear company Areva and construction firm Vinci. Among the hostages are an Areva staff member, his spouse, and five subcontractors. A spokesperson for President Nicolas Sarkozy's office stated France remains 'open to dialogue' regarding the captives' release. Audio recordings reveal four men and one woman providing personal details including names, ages (ranging 25-62), and French hometowns. The photo depicts seven individuals seated on ground, with one face obscured. Armed, masked figures stand behind them. Areva and Vinci officials confirmed enhanced security protocols for Niger-based staff and coordination with French and Nigerien authorities. French military aircraft are conducting reconnaissance flights from Niamey airport. Areva has operated uranium mines in Niger for 40 years - a resource-rich nation ranking among the world's poorest. This incident follows July's execution of French national Michel Germaneau in Mauritania by AQIM, which displayed his photo alongside French and terrorist flags in a propaganda video.
translated_content: பாரிஸ், பிரான்ஸ் (சிஎன்என்) -- நைஜரில் கைதிகளாக உள்ள ஏழு பேரின் புகைப்படம் உண்மையானது என பிரெஞ்சு வெளியுறவுத் துறை வியாழக்கிழமை உறுதி செய்தது. இதில் ஐந்து பிரெஞ்சு குடிமக்கள் உள்ளனர். இது ஒரு 'உற்சாகமான அறிகுறி' என அமைச்சகம் குறிப்பிட்டது. 'புகைப்படத்தின் எடுக்கப்பட்ட தேதி தெரியவில்லை எனினும், செப்டம்பர் 30 நிலவரப்படி அனைவரும் உயிருடன் உள்ளனர். விடுவிப்பிற்கான அனைத்து முயற்சிகளும் நடைபெறுகின்றன' என அறிவித்தது. இந்த படம் அல்-காயிதா தொடர்புடைய வலைத்தளத்தில் தோன்றியது, கைதிகள் அடையாளம் காணப்படாத ஒரு விசாரணையாளரின் கேள்விகளுக்கு பதிலளிக்கும் ஒலிப்பதிவுடன் சேர்த்து வெளியானது. இஸ்லாமிய மக்ரிப்பில் அல்-காயிதா (AQIM) இந்த கடத்தலுக்கு பொறுப்பேற்றுக்கொண்டது. பிரெஞ்சு அணுசக்தி நிறுவனமான அரேவா மற்றும் கட்டுமான நிறுவனம் வின்சியின் ஊழியர்களான ஆறு ஆண்கள் மற்றும் ஒரு பெண் இக்குழுவில் உள்ளனர். குடியரசுத் தலைவர் நிக்கோலா சர்கோசியின் அலுவலகத் தலைவர் 'விடுவிப்பு பேச்சுவார்த்தைக்கு தயார்' என தெரிவித்தார். ஒலிப்பதிவுகளில் நான்கு ஆண்களும் ஒரு பெண்ணும் தங்கள் விவரங்களைக் கொடுக்கக் கேட்கப்படுகிறார்கள். புகைப்படத்தில் முகம் மறைக்கப்பட்ட ஒருவரைத் தவிர ஏழு பேர் தரையில் அமர்ந்த நிலையில் காணப்படுகிறார்கள். ஆயுதம் தாங்கிய முகமூடி அணிந்தவர்கள் பின்னால் நிற்கின்றனர். அரேவா மற்றும் வின்சி நிறுவனங்கள் நைஜர் பணியாளர்களுக்கான பாதுகாப்பு நடவடிக்கைகளை மேம்படுத்தியுள்ளதாகவும், பிரெஞ்சு-நைஜர் அதிகாரிகளுடன் ஒத்துழைப்பதாகவும் தெரிவித்தன. பிரெஞ்சு இராணுவ விமானங்கள் நியாமி விமானநிலையத்தில் இருந்து கண்காணிப்பு பறப்புகளை மேற்கொண்டுள்ளன. உலகின் மிக வறிய நாடுகளில் ஒன்றான நைஜரில் 40 ஆண்டுகளாக அரேவா யுரேனியம் சுரங்கங்களை இயக்கிவருகிறது. AQIM ஜூலையில் மொரிட்டானியாவில் பிரெஞ்சு குடிமகன் மைக்கேல் ஜெர்மனோவைக் கொன்றது. பிரெஞ்சு மற்றும் தீவிரவாதக் கொடிகளுடன் அவரது படத்தை ஒரு வீடியோவில் காட்டியது.

article_content: Father Christmas's new Gadget Sleigh 900 (GS-900), designed by UK-based Metals4U, features modern upgrades including GPS navigation, hybrid rocket boosters, and a polycarbonate windshield. article_content: Premier League footballer Peter Crouch has been disqualified from driving for six months after accumulating 21 penalty points. The Stoke City striker's Range Rover was recorded at 69mph in a 40mph zone in March 2012 and 70mph in another 40mph zone in April 2012. Under the UK's totting-up procedure, Crouch received an automatic ban following multiple offenses. Nuneaton Magistrates' Court fined Crouch £1,300 for failing to identify the driver during two M42/M6 Toll Road speeding incidents. The 31-year-old, who already had nine penalty points, accrued 12 additional points and £485 in combined court costs and surcharges. In a separate August 2012 case, he received five more points and a £1,000 fine for post-match speeding in Macclesfield.

article_content: The FDA issued updated guidance Thursday urging consumers to discontinue use of specific batches of generic cholesterol medication atorvastatin due to potential glass contamination. This follows Ranbaxy Pharmaceuticals' recall of 41 product lots initiated three weeks prior, marking the first official consumer warning from regulators. Despite the FDA's alert, some pharmacies continue advising patients that remaining medication is safe. Express Scripts stated it wouldn't offer refunds and recommended continued use, while CVS offered replacements only upon request. Consumer Reports' Lisa Gill criticized the FDA's three-week delay in issuing guidance as 'confusing' and 'surprising'. The FDA clarified that contaminating glass particles are sand-sized and pose low health risks, but advised patients to contact pharmacies about lot numbers - a process pharmacists describe as challenging. Ranbaxy (India's largest pharmaceutical company and 12th-largest global generics manufacturer), which paused production during investigation, has a history of quality violations including a 2008 FDA import ban over fraudulent testing practices.

article_content: Millions of travelers affected by flight delays can now claim compensation following landmark UK Supreme Court rulings. Valid claims may date back six years, overcoming previous airline objections. The court rejected appeals from Jet2 and Thomson Airways, potentially enabling £3.89bn in historical payouts. Under EU Regulation EC 261/2004, passengers experiencing delays exceeding three hours due to technical faults can claim up to £470. Airlines previously avoided compensation by citing 'extraordinary circumstances,' but courts now classify technical issues as standard operational responsibilities. Key cases involved Ronald Huzar's 27-hour Jet2 delay (2011 Malaga-Manchester) and James Dawson's 2006 Thomson delay (Gatwick-Dominican Republic). Both won through multiple court levels, with Supreme Court rejecting final appeals. Huzar received £940 compensation; Dawson obtained £1,488.73 including interest. The Civil Aviation Authority has directed airlines to process paused claims. Thomson Airways expressed disappointment, while Jet2 declined comment. Legal analysts predict surge in claims following these precedents.

article_content: (CNN) -- Chelsea defender Ashley Cole has been charged by the Football Association (FA) following a Twitter post where he called the organization 'a bunch of twats.' This occurred after an FA panel investigating John Terry's racial abuse case questioned Cole's testimony. Terry, who retired from international football, was found guilty by the FA of racially abusing QPR's Anton Ferdinand, receiving a four-match ban and $350,000 fine. Cole's tweet responded to claims he altered evidence: 'Hahahahaa, well done #fa I lied did I, #BUNCHOFTWATS.' He apologized hours later but now faces misconduct charges. The FA stated the tweet was 'improper and/or brought the game into disrepute,' with a response deadline of October 11, 2012. The FA panel expressed 'considerable doubt' about whether Cole's amended statement - modified by Chelsea secretary Dave Barnard to include 'black' - reflected his original account. Chelsea manager Roberto Di Matteo confirmed Cole violated club social media policies, noting players 'represent employers and governing bodies.'

article_content: UK Parliament Speaker John Bercow faces renewed scrutiny following internal disputes over a high-profile appointment. Conservative MP Michael Fabricant disclosed receiving messages from parliamentary staff containing strong criticism of Bercow's leadership during the controversial selection process for Clerk of the Commons. The constitutional position, requiring formal approval through Royal Letters Patent, became contentious when Bercow proposed both splitting the historic role and nominating Australian official Carol Mills. Parliamentary records confirm the selection panel implemented a temporary pause in deliberations after lawmakers raised concerns about recruitment procedures. Fabricant asserted external consultants from Saxton Bampfylde were restricted from fully presenting candidate information, though Bercow refuted these claims during heated Commons exchanges. The Speaker maintained that proper protocols were followed, stating 'the panel made its judgment based on comprehensive materials.' Tensions escalated as multiple MPs challenged procedural decisions, including panel composition changes that replaced Deputy Speaker Lindsay Hoyle with Labour's Margaret Hodge. Bercow dismissed conflict-of-interest concerns regarding Hodge's Public Accounts Committee role, asserting all processes met parliamentary standards. The £200,000 annual position remains vacant as constitutional debates continue regarding modernization of this key parliamentary office.

article_content: A Staffordshire Bull Terrier named Chance has been reunited with his family after 10 years missing, saved from euthanasia by a microchip scan. The dog disappeared from owner Sion Cox's Barry garden in 2004 when Sion was 11. Despite exhaustive searches, the family eventually adopted another pet. Found malnourished in a Newport underpass (20 miles away) in 2014, Chance was scheduled for euthanasia at Coronation Kennels due to his age and health. A routine microchip check revealed owner Julie Coombes' details, enabling a tearful reunion. Now 21, Sion cares for the 13-year-old dog in Cardiff, noting Chance's immediate recognition of family members. Kennel staff confirmed this as their longest separation case. Julie recalled: 'We'd microchipped him as a puppy - that tiny chip saved his life.' Despite arthritis and neglect-related health issues, Chance enjoys walks and stable home life with his original family.

article_content: AC Milan has achieved its first profitable fiscal year since 2006, announcing a €6.1 million surplus for 2022-23. The club's resurgence follows strategic cost management by American investors, including RedBird Capital Partners who acquired majority ownership in August 2022 for €1.2 billion. Revenue growth exceeded €400 million - a record high - marking significant improvement from previous management eras, including Chinese ownership that ended in 2018. Sporting success accompanied financial recovery, with the team claiming the 2021-22 Serie A title and reaching last season's Champions League semifinals. Tonight's match against PSG carries both sporting and financial implications, as European competition earnings contributed €80 million to last year's revenue through various performance bonuses.

article_content: (CNN) -- Mark Kessler, the Pennsylvania police chief who gained attention for videos showing him firing automatic weapons while criticizing gun control measures, has received a termination notice. The Gilberton Borough Council voted 6-1 to dismiss him during a Thursday night meeting, according to council chairman Daniel J. Malloy. Kessler, initially suspended on July 31 amid a large protest involving thousands of supporters (some openly armed) in Schuylkill County, will remain suspended for 10 days pending appeal. Malloy declined further comment. 'We anticipated this outcome,' Kessler told CNN affiliate WFMZ-TV following the vote. His attorney Joseph Nahas confirmed plans to request a public hearing next week. The council cited allegations of borough property misuse, duty neglect, and failure to return weapons as grounds for termination. Kessler maintains his dismissal stems from viral videos where he criticized liberal gun policies and challenged Secretary of State John Kerry regarding firearm regulations, including one instance where he dared Kerry to confiscate his weapons. article_content: The vibrant colors in Anas Homsi's 'Play in the City' initially suggest cheerfulness, but the painting's true subject is human conflict. 'This figure wants to kill,' Homsi explains, pointing to a menacing form, 'while this one tries to prevent it.' His work, inspired by Syria's civil war, forms part of the 'True Colors' exhibition at Beirut's Joanna Seikaly Gallery. Alongside fellow Syrian artists Wissam Shaabi and Fadi Al-Hamwi, Homsi explores war's impact through themes of survival and societal breakdown. 'Violence drives my creative process,' says Homsi, whose recent works reflect the shock of learning about relatives' executions. The artists, all University of Damascus Fine Arts alumni, found Beirut's galleries crucial for showcasing work after Syria's art scene collapsed. Gallery owner Joanna Seikaly notes: 'Lebanon's art community benefits from displaced Syrian talent while highlighting their homeland's crisis.' Shaabi's 'City of Hope' depicts peaceful urban life with symbolic religious coexistence through crescent and cross motifs. 'Art carries messages of hope,' he states. Contrastingly, Al-Hamwi's 'Stinkbomb' captures Damascus' daily dread, showing a gas-masked figure clutching a rose. As the only artist still in Syria, he admits: 'Some days I question if art matters - but documenting our reality remains essential.'

article_content: Raja Aboutarik, 56, fraudulently obtained £13,052 in UK housing and council tax benefits for a Notting Hill property between May 2006-May 2011 while concurrently receiving approximately £45,000 in French state benefits. West London Magistrates' Court heard the dual claims ended when French authorities verified her Paris residence. Aboutarik, who attributes her unemployment to alcohol dependency and partial arm paralysis from childhood, was ordered to repay £20 weekly. District Judge James Henderson issued an 8-week suspended sentence with 3-month curfew, citing mitigating health factors including diabetes and memory impairment from a past assault.

article_content: Fourteen-year-old Paris Jackson expressed urgent concern Sunday about the disappearance of her grandmother Katherine Jackson, the family matriarch who's raised her since Michael Jackson's 2009 death. Through social media posts, Paris revealed she hadn't communicated with Katherine for seven days, contradicting claims from uncles Jermaine and Randy Jackson that their 82-year-old mother was resting under medical care in Arizona. Legal representative Sandra Ribera disclosed that Katherine Jackson reportedly left her California home July 15 with daughter Rebbie after physician Dr. Allan Metzger - who testified for convicted physician Conrad Murray during Michael Jackson's involuntary manslaughter trial - advised against traveling by recreational vehicle. Despite plans to attend a New Mexico concert, Katherine never arrived at the event. Family tensions escalated as Paris publicly shared her bodyguard's contact information, urging followers to alert authorities if spotting her grandmother. Ribera noted Katherine's unprecedented week-long communication blackout, stating: 'She's never gone 24 hours without contacting her children. We're deeply concerned about her welfare.' article_content: Everton manager Roberto Martinez praised his team's resilience in securing a 1-1 Europa League draw against FK Krasnodar, describing it as an 'incredible result' and valuable learning experience. Despite being outplayed for much of the Group H match at Kuban Stadium, veteran striker Samuel Eto'o equalized in the 82nd minute after Ari's 43rd-minute opener for the hosts. Martinez emphasized the team's development: 'Today gave us crucial experience. Krasnodar started stronger, but we improved. While a draw is fair, they missed key chances.' The Spanish coach leveraged Eto'o and Aiden McGeady's knowledge of Russian football in pre-match preparations. Eto'o, utilizing his three-time Champions League-winning experience, clinically converted Leighton Baines' cross late in the game. Martinez applauded the striker's composure: 'He waited patiently and delivered top-quality finishing - exactly why his experience matters.' Everton now leads Group H with four points from two matches, ahead of Krasnodar and Lille (2 points each) and Wolfsburg (1 point).

article_content: (CNN) -- A Connecticut paramedic faces charges for allegedly sexually assaulting a semi-conscious patient during ambulance transport last month, according to police. Mark Powell, 49, surrendered to authorities Thursday and was charged with first-degree sexual assault and unlawful restraint, Hamden Police Capt. Ronald Smith confirmed. The 22-year-old woman required emergency treatment after sustaining a head injury on December 25. Authorities state the alleged assault occurred while she was restrained on a stretcher en route to Yale-New Haven Hospital. The victim delayed reporting the incident for three days due to embarrassment and fear, Smith said. American Medical Response (AMR) placed Powell on administrative leave, stating: 'We take patient safety seriously and do not tolerate abusive behavior,' according to General Manager Charles Babson. Powell was released after posting $25,000 bond and is scheduled to appear in court January 19. His legal representation status remains unconfirmed.

article_content: The Khayal family's fate remains unknown after their failed escape attempt during Gaza's November 10 four-hour evacuation window. Dina Alalami, a Qatari resident, lost contact six days ago following Israeli tank fire that killed multiple relatives. Over 11,500 Palestinians have died in the conflict, including women and children. Evacuating with white flags as Israeli forces advanced, the family faced direct fire on Shuhada Street. Lina Khayal died instantly from chest wounds while sister Rulla and injured relatives sheltered in the Bakri building. Their final message - 'We are alive' - preceded communication blackout. Dina, now in Cairo, mourns: 'My sister's body lies unburied - this indignity breaks us.' 'We're not just improving treatments, but revolutionizing patient journeys using AI-powered precision,' he explained. The 'Snackable AI' system provides unfiltered operational data through Instagram-style reels, bypassing traditional slide reports. Sanofi's $1 billion Suzhou research hub, a 30-minute train ride from Shanghai, operates at 'Gigafactory' intensity according to insiders. This contrasts with competitors' reduced Chinese R&D presence. Leadership changes include elevating immunology pioneer Dr. Frank Nestle to CSO and appointing biotech veteran Dr. Houman Ashrafian to lead R&D. While short-term investors balk at R&D costs, Hudson cites Dupixent - their $10 billion first-in-class immunology drug - as proof of strategy. 'We're building medicine's future through AI and biologics, even if it means short-term pain,' he concluded, highlighting 83% employee adoption of new AI tools.

article_content: Recent research highlights alarming sexual health patterns among university students. A ShagAtUni.com survey of 2,177 graduates found 23% contracted sexually transmitted infections (STIs) during their first year, with 89% reporting inconsistent condom use. Alcohol consumption preceded 73% of sexual encounters. The study revealed variations across disciplines: Theatre arts students reported the highest average of 28 sexual partners, followed by dance (25) and media studies (22). Law and geography students reported the lowest averages at 11 and 10 partners respectively. Public Health England's data indicates a 50% increase in STI rates among under-25s since 2003, with 448,422 new cases recorded in 2012. Chlamydia constitutes 60% of student STI cases. Health authorities warn that 67% of respondents prioritize sexual activity over condom use, particularly concerning given emerging antibiotic-resistant gonorrhoea strains.

article_content: By Sean Poulter, Consumer Affairs Editor. London house prices are increasing by over 20% annually, raising concerns about a potential housing bubble. Data from the Land Registry shows some boroughs have seen values rise by nearly £100,000 in one year, with the surge affecting surrounding South East regions. The average London home now costs £414,356, reflecting a 13.8% yearly increase. This boom is making homeownership inaccessible for many, forcing buyers to take on large mortgages that may become unaffordable if interest rates rise. In Hackney, east London, average prices jumped 21.5% to £528,737 – a £93,500 annual increase. Waltham Forest saw 20.1% growth, while Islington recorded 17.7%. Kensington and Chelsea remain the UK's most expensive area, with average prices at £1.24 million (14.8% increase), partly driven by wealthy international buyers. The London effect has pushed prices up 6% in Hertfordshire, Surrey, and Reading. However, prices declined in parts of North East England and Wales. Nationally, prices rose 5.3%, averaging £170,000 across England and Wales. The Bank of England warns about risky high-income multiple mortgages, with 1 in 5 London borrowers taking loans over four times their income. Prince Charles cautioned that the bubble could exclude young buyers from London's market. Economist Ed Stansfield of Capital Economics questioned whether the Bank can prevent boom-bust cycles while maintaining low rates. Martin Stewart, director of London Money, noted: 'London prices have lost touch with reality, driven by overseas investors using property as capital protection, pricing out local residents.'

article_content: Britain's former Director of Public Prosecutions has called for criminal penalties against professionals who fail to report child abuse suspicions, responding to systemic failures revealed by the Jimmy Savile case. Keir Starmer QC emphasized the need for 'explicit legal requirements rather than vague guidelines' during a BBC Panorama appearance, highlighting Washington State's mandatory reporting framework as a potential model. Liz Dux, legal representative for over 70 Savile survivors, stated: 'While reporting processes have improved since 2013, only legal mandates can prevent institutional inaction.' The Mandate Now coalition - including major abuse charities - specifically targets schools and care providers, demanding legal accountability. Contrary to these calls, the Department for Education argues mandatory reporting could 'overburden systems and reduce effectiveness,' citing international case studies.

article_content: By Lydia Warren for MailOnline and Associated Press. Kevin Ward Jr.'s family discovered his death through Facebook, his father revealed. Speaking publicly for the first time since the 20-year-old was struck by NASCAR champion Tony Stewart at Canandaigua Motorsports Park, Kevin Ward Sr. stated his daughter learned the tragic news online while they awaited updates at the hospital. 'He was divinely gifted,' Ward Sr. told Syracuse.com. 'I believe he died content.' Ward Sr. expressed frustration toward Stewart, noting only the driver knows the full truth about the August 9 incident. 'The person who knows what happened might face prison. Will he confess?' he asked. The parents witnessed emergency workers' 45-minute resuscitation attempt before their daughter's call confirmed the worst. Video evidence shows Stewart's car contacting Ward's vehicle before the crash. Ward exited his car and gestured toward passing vehicles before being struck by Stewart's right rear tire. Ward Sr. emphasized this was his son's first mid-race exit, attributing it to 'who forced him into the wall.' Legal experts including Corey Rayburn Yung of Kansas University School of Law suggest Stewart could face second-degree manslaughter charges if prosecutors prove recklessness. Sheriff Philip Povero's investigation continues, reviewing multiple videos and witness accounts. A 1949 Massachusetts legal precedent involving racer Joseph Sostilio was referenced regarding track conduct liability. Ward Jr.'s funeral occurred Thursday. While no criminal intent was initially found, civil liability remains possible. Sheriff Povero confirmed evidence will be forwarded to the district attorney post-investigation.

article_content: The U.S. military has officially removed gender barriers for frontline combat positions, a historic shift influenced by Gen. Martin Dempsey's formative 2003 Iraq deployment. While inspecting his security detail in Baghdad, Dempsey encountered a female turret gunner named Amanda - an experience he credits as pivotal in recognizing women's battlefield capabilities. Defense Secretary Leon Panetta announced the policy change alongside Dempsey, noting that over 200,000 active-duty women can now qualify for previously restricted roles. 'This acknowledges reality,' Panetta stated, referencing women's unofficial combat participation during recent conflicts. Official data shows 67 women killed in hostile fire in Iraq and 33 in combat zones of Afghanistan since 2001. While the 1994 combat exclusion policy is being phased out, military leaders stress that rigorous physical standards won't be compromised. Army Training Command chief Gen. Robert Cone outlined new fitness benchmarks: 'Prospective infantry must lift 54 pounds overhead and carry 66-pound packs.' The transition period extends through January 2016, with each branch developing implementation timelines. Reactions remain mixed. Supporters like Congresswoman Tulsi Gabbard highlight exemplary female soldiers, including post-WWII Silver Star recipients. article_content: Health authorities in South Wales are racing to contain a measles outbreak with emergency vaccination clinics drawing large crowds. Over 1,000 concerned parents queued at hospitals in Swansea this weekend following warnings about 588 confirmed cases in the region. Public health data shows 40 new infections emerged just since Wednesday, with daily reports averaging 20 cases. Dr. Marion Lyons of Public Health Wales stressed the urgency: 'With nearly 3,800 children remaining unvaccinated in Swansea, we're seeing preventable infections spread rapidly. The two-dose MMR regimen provides 99% protection - it's our best defense. Infants aged 6-12 months in outbreak zones can receive early doses through their GPs.' Four area hospitals extended weekend hours for walk-in vaccinations, prioritizing children but welcoming all unvaccinated individuals. Recent clinic visits show promising response, with 586 unscheduled MMR doses administered last week. However, officials warn the outbreak may persist through summer without broader immunization. Specialists note measles poses particular risks to vulnerable groups including infants, cancer patients, and pregnant women.

article_content: Watumiaji wa Twitter wameunga mkono hatua ya wasichana watatu waliochukulia picha za rais wa Burundi Pierre Nkurunziza na kuziharibu kwa kuchora. Picha zilizoharibiwa zimesambaa kwenye mitandao ya kijamii chini ya hashtag #FreeOurGirls. Wasichana hao walishtakiwa wiki iliopita kwa kosa la kumtusi rais na wanakabiliwa na kifungo cha miaka mitano. Mamlaka za Burundi zinashutumiwa kwa ukiukaji wa haki za binadamu. Wasichana walio na umri wa miaka 15, 16, na 17 walikamatwa wiki mbili zilizopita baada ya kuchora picha za rais kwenye vitabu vyao. Wanafunzi wanne waliokamatwa pamoja nao waliachiliwa. Baba wa mmoja wa wasichana alisema kwa Human Rights Watch kwamba walikuwa na wasiwasi wa chakula. HRW imetaka serikali iwaache wasichana na kukabiliana na ukatili wa vikosi vya usalama. Lewis Mudge wa HRW alisema serikali inapaswa kuwakamata wauaji wa haki za binadamu badala ya wasichana. Mwaka 2016, wasichana wengi walifungwa na wengine walipewa kifungo kwa kuchora picha za rais.
translated_content: Twitter users have shown support for three Burundian schoolgirls who drew on images of President Pierre Nkurunziza. The altered presidential photos circulated widely on social media with the hashtag #FreeOurGirls. The teenagers, aged 15-17, face charges of insulting the head of state and potential five-year jail terms. Burundian authorities face ongoing criticism over human rights concerns. Arrested two weeks ago for doodling on textbook images of the president, the girls saw four co-detained classmates later released. A parent revealed to Human Rights Watch about their food security fears. HRW has urged the government to free the girls and curb security force abuses. HRW's Lewis Mudge emphasized prosecuting serious rights violators over punishing students. This echoes a 2016 incident where girls were jailed and students expelled for similar acts of political expression.
